main_text.head: Quæstio XIII.
An suam Patriam suosque cives, apud exteros laudare conveniat?
main_text.p: G Estat pietatis indubitatam tesseram, quem suorum tangit honos, quem Patriæ suæ decus irrequietis adurget stimulis, ut impatiens moræ, involet in munia Famæ non satis officiosæ, & meritam suis pompam apud exteros ducat zelosus apparitor: Atque interim arctas ipse sibi leges dictat, paria iis, quæ laudat, præstandi: turpe enim erit, si degener, si indignus laudatâ patriâ judicetur ipse laudator. Adde præconium istud, quod plenis buccis in Patriam difflamus, in nos ipsos provolvi latente ductu: Et cùm alibi sua-
main_text.notes: The initial G is a large woodcut letter, joined to "Estat". The last word "sua-" is a line-end hyphenated word ("suas-"/"suasu" continuing on the next page); the final letters are partly obscured. Show-through from the facing page is present in the background and was not transcribed.
